items.followUp: Define boiling point and describe two factors that affect it.

rubric.why: The definition must identify vapour pressure as the pressure of a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the pressure exerted by the vapour and its equilibrium with the liquid.

rubric.why: Increasing temperature allows more molecules to escape from the liquid into the vapour phase.
rubric.description: States that vapour pressure increases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction of the temperature effect.

rubric.why: Liquids with weaker intermolecular attractions vaporize more readily and have higher vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Describes how the nature of the liquid affects vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct relationship between intermolecular forces and vapour pressure.

rubric.why: A dissolved non-volatile impurity reduces the tendency of solvent molecules to escape into the vapour phase.
rubric.description: States that a dissolved non-volatile impurity lowers vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect of a non-volatile impurity or solute.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour when it is in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed container.
An increase in temperature increases vapour pressure because more molecules escape from the liquid into the vapour phase.
The nature of the liquid affects vapour pressure: weaker intermolecular forces give higher vapour pressure, while stronger intermolecular forces give lower vapour pressure.
A dissolved non volatile impurity lowers the vapour pressure of the liquid.
